items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 8:5:1
items.html:
The Mochin of AK with the aspect of the Taamim of SAG: And although all of Nekudim, even the first Rosh in them, is extended from the Nekudot of SAG — so that the MAN should have had to rise only as far as the Nekudot in the Rosh of SAG — indeed in truth they rose to the Nekudot of SAG. But since with this ascent of theirs the coupling of AB-SAG took place, in which the illumination of AB that reached SAG lowered the bottom Hey from the Einayim of SAG to the Peh of SAG, by which the AHP that had gone out of the Rosh of SAG rejoin and return to the aspect of a Rosh, the Nekudot of SAG are found joining with the Taamim of SAG into a single degree. And then the Nekudot of SAG are no longer reckoned by a name, for they are nullified in the higher phase within them, which is the Taamim. Therefore the raising of MAN too is regarded as having risen to the Taamim, since the Nekudot are not reckoned by a name, being nullified in them, as the ARI writes above (page 396, item 6, study it there well).
And know that from here comes out the rule that every raising of MAN is from a lower one to the upper of its upper one, and the upper of the upper corrects them for the sake of the upper one. For ZON raise the MAN for the sake of their upper one, which is YESHSUT, to the upper of the upper, which is AVI, and AVI correct them for the sake of YESHSUT. And so it is in all the degrees. This is because every raising of MAN causes the bottom Hey to descend from the Nikvey Einayim downward, and through this one acquires the GAR. Thus, at the time when ZON raise the MAN of YESHSUT, they thereby cause the bottom Hey to descend from the Einayim of AVI downward, and then YESHSUT is found joining with AVI into a single degree, and YESHSUT acquires its GAR, meaning the aspect of AVI. And you see that the MAN that ZON raised for the need of YESHSUT rose to the phases of AVI, that is, to the bottom Hey in the Einayim of AVI, which they lowered downward, and thereby corrected the Mochin of YESHSUT. Thus the lower one raised the MAN for the sake of its upper one, which is YESHSUT, to the upper of its upper, which is AVI; and AVI coupled together upon that MAN and lowered the bottom Hey from their Einayim downward, and thereby joined YESHSUT to their own degree, and YESHSUT acquired its GAR. With this you will understand what the ARI likens there (page 396, item 6), comparing AB and SAG to AVI and YESHSUT. See there.
And this matter began with the first raising of MAN that took place in the worlds, which is the raising of MAN of the inner NHY of AK to the Taamim of the Rosh of SAG, spoken of in the above words of the ARI on page 396. For there it lowered the bottom Hey from the Einayim to the Peh of SAG, as above at the beginning of this item. Here, however, since the bottom Hey had risen to Keter, which is the secret of the forehead, the bottom Hey therefore descended from the forehead to the Peh, as written further along.
And this is what he says, “that through the raising of MAN of the seven lights the aspect of HaVaYaH of AB of Yudin, which is the whole of the aspect of the Mochin of AK, coupled with the aspect of the Taamim of SAG, which are AHP.” For the Rosh of SAG is called by the name Ozen [ear], Hotem [nose], Peh [mouth], since the highest phase in it is the light of the Ozen, meaning Bina. And it clothes the Partzuf AB of AK from the Chazeh [chest] upward, as far as the Peh of AB. Therefore the HGT of AB of AK are regarded as the phases of Mochin for SAG, and also for the whole of the Mochin that are extended from AK; for the first Partzuf of AK is exalted above the worlds, and they do not illuminate except by way of the HGT of AB, which are the Mochin of SAG of AK. And after the illumination of the Mochin from this AB is extended to the Rosh of SAG, meaning to the Taamim, then the bottom Hey descends from the forehead to the Peh, as written.

items.html:
The Taamim of SAG had no shattering in them at all: And you must know here that the secret of the breaking begins even before the world of Nekudim, namely in the nine lower ones of the Partzuf SAG of AK, called the Nekudot of SAG, which expanded from the Tabur of SAG downward, to the end of his legs, as above in the words of the ARI (page 393, item 3). For since they expanded from the Tabur downward, into the place of the inner NHY of AK, they therefore became mixed with phase four, and this brought about the second restriction in the worlds, called the restriction of the NHY of AK. For because of the mixing of phase two, which is Bina, with phase four, which is Malchut, Bina received the aspect of the restriction that is in Malchut. Therefore Bina and ZON went outside of all the degrees: the AHP of the Rosh went out to the aspect of a Guf; the Bina and ZON of the Guf went out to the aspect of the NHY below the Tabur; and the Bina and ZON of the ten Sefirot of NHY went out entirely, outside of Atzilut, and became BYA of separation.
Thus in SAG too the Bina and ZON of the NHY went out and fell into BYA, in the likeness of the breaking of the vessels. However, this occurred only in the Nekudot of SAG, which expanded from the Tabur downward and became mixed with the bottom Hey, as above; but it has no bearing whatsoever upon the upper half of SAG, called the Taamim, which end above the Tabur of AK. And this is what he says, “that the raising of MAN was to the Taamim of SAG, in which there was no breaking at all,” as explained.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 8:5:3
items.html:
That emerge from the breath of AHP — but only the aspect of their very essence and their internality: For there are two kinds of AHP. The first is the Rosh of SAG, called the Taamim of SAG, which, since its level reaches as far as Bina, is called by the name AHP. And the second is the breaths of AHP that went outside the degree, as above, and are regarded as branches that go out from SAG, which are the hairs of the Dikna [beard] of SAG, and they become the roots of the GAR of Nekudim, as above in the words of the ARI (page 394, item 4). And this is what he says, that the coupling of AB was with the AHP that are the Taamim of SAG, and not with the Partzuf of the hairs that went outside, which are the phases of the Nekudot of the Rosh of SAG, in which there was breaking, as above.
And although the upper one that relates to the ten Sefirot of Nekudim is only the Nekudot of SAG, meaning the hairs of the Dikna, as above, nevertheless they are nullified in the Taamim of SAG and are not reckoned by a name at all, for the coupling of AB joins them to the degree of the Rosh of SAG at the time of the coupling, as above (page 601, the passage beginning “The Mochin of AK,” see there).
